scenarios.decisive_discriminator: Regional ST depression with T-wave inversion that deepens on a repeat tracing, together with a rising high-sensitivity troponin, places acute myocardial injury in an ischaemic context; every feature that would carry the presentation to a non-ischaemic cause is positively reported against.

scenarios.stem: A 58-year-old man describes 90 minutes of heavy retrosternal pressure that began while he was climbing stairs and has eased only slightly with rest. He is diaphoretic. Blood pressure is 148/86 mmHg and equal in both arms, heart rate is 92 beats/min, respiratory rate is 16 breaths/min and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The discomfort is not sharp, does not change with posture or deep inspiration, and he has no heartburn or regurgitation. His chest is clear, his calves are soft and he has had no recent immobility, surgery or travel. There is no back pain and no pulse deficit. The electrocardiogram shows horizontal ST depression with T-wave inversion across the lateral precordial leads, and a tracing repeated twenty minutes later shows the depression has deepened. The initial high-sensitivity troponin is above the upper reference limit and the repeat value is higher.

scenarios.stem: A 7-month-old boy is brought to the clinic in the third day of an illness that began with fever, cough and a runny nose and has since progressed to noisy, faster breathing. This is the first time he has ever wheezed. He was born at term, has no eczema or other atopy and there is no family history of asthma. There was no choking episode and nothing was seen in his mouth. His temperature is 38.1 degrees Celsius, his respiratory rate is 52 breaths/min and his oxygen saturation is 94% in room air. On auscultation there is widespread symmetric expiratory wheeze with fine crackles in both lung fields and air entry is equal throughout, with no focal area of reduced or altered air entry. scenarios.stem: A province evaluates a cancer screening programme. Participants were randomly allocated to be invited or not invited, and the two groups were comparable at baseline. After twelve years the cumulative number of people diagnosed with the cancer is the same in both groups, and the number of deaths from the cancer is also the same in both groups. Among those diagnosed, however, mean survival measured from the date of diagnosis is four years longer in the invited group than in the group that was not invited. The pathology review found the same distribution of tumour grades and growth rates in the two groups. The programme cites the survival figure as evidence of its success.

scenarios.decisive_discriminator: A relative figure without a denominator or a statement of harms cannot support an informed choice, so the revision that protects autonomy is the one that replaces it with the absolute chance of benefit alongside the commonest harm.
scenarios.key_option_text: Replace the relative benefit figure with the absolute chance of benefit and the chance of a false positive result
scenarios.lead_in: Which revision to the letter would best protect the autonomy of the people invited?
scenarios.stem: A provincial screening programme is revising the letter that invites eligible residents to attend. The programme has stated that the objective of this revision is to protect the autonomy of the people invited, and that raising uptake is explicitly not the objective of this revision. The present letter states only that screening reduces the risk of dying from the disease by thirty per cent. It gives no absolute figures, no denominator, and no description of the harms of screening. The audience is the general adult population of the province, whose numeracy the programme's own testing found to be limited, so figures expressing test performance are not reliably interpreted by the readers.

scenarios.lead_in: What should the programme do about the planned launch?
scenarios.stem: A regional health authority plans to launch a population screening programme next month. The test is accurate and its cut-off has been validated in this population, and modelling shows it sits appropriately between the low-risk and high-risk ends of the scale. The programme has written goals and an evaluation plan, and a completed economic evaluation shows it to be good value for money. However, the region has one diagnostic clinic for confirmatory testing, its current waiting time is fourteen months, and there is no funded pathway to treatment for those confirmed. The authority has costed the additional capacity and has the money, but the staff have not yet been recruited and the clinic space is not yet built.

Attendance was entirely voluntary and no one was allocated to a group. After ten years the attenders have lower mortality from the screened disease and also lower mortality from causes the programme cannot affect, including road traffic collisions. The attenders were less likely to smoke and more likely to exercise at baseline. The cumulative number of people diagnosed with the disease is the same in both groups, the distribution of tumour grades and growth rates is the same, and survival measured from diagnosis does not differ between the groups.

scenarios.stem: A 59-year-old man is admitted with a severe major depressive episode. He is convinced, against all evidence, that his internal organs have rotted away and that he is being punished, and he cannot be reasoned out of this belief. He is eating and drinking, is not physically deteriorating and has no suicidal intent, and admission has already secured his safety. He has had no previous psychiatric treatment and has no contraindication to any of the agents under consideration. Physical examination, thyroid function and a complete blood count are normal.

scenarios.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?
scenarios.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with eighteen hours of abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus and has since settled in the right lower quadrant. She has been off her food and has vomited twice. Her temperature is 38.0 degrees Celsius and her white cell count is 14.2 x 10^9/L with a left shift. On examination she has right lower quadrant tenderness with rebound. Pelvic examination is unremarkable: there is no cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal tenderness and no abnormal discharge. A urine pregnancy test is negative and urinalysis shows no blood. She has no flank or groin pain. She has never had pelvic pain before and her last menstrual period was two weeks ago; there is no known adnexal mass and no previous pelvic imaging.

scenarios.stem: A 47-year-old man with a body mass index of 34 kg/m2 has had twelve hours of right lower quadrant pain with anorexia and one episode of vomiting. His temperature is 37.6 degrees Celsius and his white cell count is 11.8 x 10^9/L. He has right lower quadrant tenderness without guarding or rebound, and the surgical team records the clinical probability of appendicitis as intermediate rather than high. No imaging has been performed. He is haemodynamically stable and computed tomography, ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging are all available immediately.

scenarios.lead_in: Which management strategy is most appropriate?
scenarios.stem: A 34-year-old man has had eighteen hours of migratory right lower quadrant pain. His temperature is 37.9 degrees Celsius, his heart rate is 88 beats/min and his blood pressure is 126/78 mmHg. Computed tomography reports a thickened appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding, and states explicitly that there is no perforation, no free fluid, no abscess and no phlegmon. He is physiologically stable, has no cardiorespiratory disease and no contraindication to a general anaesthetic or to laparoscopy. He has been counselled about the options and has expressed no preference and has not been asked to accept any risk of recurrence.

scenarios.lead_in: What is the most appropriate disposition?
scenarios.stem: A 29-year-old woman presented with fourteen hours of right lower quadrant pain. Ultrasonography was non-diagnostic and a subsequent computed tomography scan of the abdomen was also non-diagnostic. On reassessment her temperature is 37.4 degrees Celsius, her white cell count is 10.9 x 10^9/L and her abdomen is tender in the right lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. The consultant records that clinical suspicion on reassessment is intermediate rather than high. She is haemodynamically stable and lives alone an hour from the hospital.
